title: The same field name gets two different column names depending on its nesting depth
rationale: flatten() builds a defensive copy with sanitizeKey applied, then hands that copy to flattenObject, which calls sanitizeKey AGAIN on every entry. Depth-0 keys are sanitized twice and deeper keys once. String.replace("__","_") is not idempotent on odd runs, so an identical source name at two depths produces two different names. No single-nesting-level test can see this.
catchesBugClass: Redundant application of a non-idempotent transform, producing depth-dependent output. Distinct from the collapse itself: fixing the collapse hides it, removing the duplicate call fixes it without touching the collapse.
cannotCatch: It cannot detect the redundant call in the default configuration, where sanitizeKey is effectively identity for non-empty keys. The bug is latent there and any future non-idempotent sanitizer will reintroduce it with no coverage.

predicted.detail: Two occurrences of one source name land under two different names, and neither is the original.
